title: fix-epochal-metering-drops-during-rolling-upgrades-in-private-clusters
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Several Private deployment customers reported sudden multi-hour drops in recorded token usage that did not align with request traffic. The drops correspond to nightly rolling upgrades of the private control plane in a subset of clusters using our legacy ingest proxy. Impact: undercounted usage across billing windows, customer escalations flagged by Accounts and CS. This ticket tracks diagnosis, short-term mitigation, and a verified patch to the metering pipeline to prevent future epochal drops during rolling upgrades.
reproduction_steps: 1) Stand up a private cluster with legacy-ingest-proxy enabled
2) Load sustained streaming traffic (40–60 rps) for 4+ hours
3) Trigger the control-plane rolling upgrade with default drain timeout
4) Observe metering delta stream to ingestion service during upgrade windows via debug metrics
observed_symptoms: sudden flatline in ingested token delta for tenant shards for 5–30 minutes during certain upgrade epochs
inconsistent commit acks from metering-proxy to ledger service
no client-side retry spikes (traffic still inbound)
post-upgrade backfill resumes but with missing epoch-boundary blobs
initial_findings: legacy-ingest-proxy drops batched commit windows when its local epoch counter resets during graceful restarts
metering ingestion relies on per-proxy epoch monotonicity to idempotently apply rollup blobs
on private clusters with >8 proxies the reset timing leads to lost commit markers for specific tenant partitions
proposed_solution: 1) Patch legacy-ingest-proxy to persist epoch counter across restarts using local disk checkpointing
2) Enhance ingestion service to tolerate epoch regressions by consulting last-seen commit id per-tenant and asking proxies to re-emit outstanding windows
3) Add end-to-end regression test that performs rolling upgrades under load and asserts no token delta loss
short_term_mitigation: Enable emergency backfill job to reconstruct missing token blobs from raw request logs for affected windows
Temporarily disable automatic rolling upgrades for private clusters with legacy proxy (config flag) until patch is rolled out
implementation_notes: Added new metric: ingest.epoch_reset_detected (counter) and ingest.window_commit_latency (histogram)
Will ship proxy patch via private agent v2.3.1 with opt-in rollout to a single pilot customer for 48h monitoring
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch persistence and startup sequence
Integration harness simulating 10 proxies and rolling restarts under load
Canary in eu-west-1 private pilot with 2 tenants; compare reported usage vs golden reference
rollback_plan: If pilot shows regression, revert proxy change and re-enable upgrade hold; run backfill job and notify customers
Maintain ability to toggle proxy epoch persistence via runtime flag for immediate rollback
acceptance_criteria: No >1% loss in reported tokens compared to golden ingestion in canary during rolling upgrades
ingest.epoch_reset_detected events are reduced to zero for patched proxies in pilot
Backfill accurately reconstructs missing usage for confirmed affected windows (manual verification by Revenue Ops)
